description: Composite group whose core is five bright-field optical micrographs (etched surface) of Fe–30Mn–11Al–1.2C low-density steel cold rolled to increasing reductions; each optical panel carries a 100 µm scale bar in its lower-right corner. (a) 10% reduction: equiaxed grains crossed by sets of fine, straight, parallel slip bands whose spacing differs from grain to grain, with a red rectangle marking a region shown enlarged in a separate red-framed inset (slip bands of two orientations crossing). (b) 30%: same slip-band character, bands more numerous and denser. (c) 50%: the rolling geometry is labelled, with a vertical arrow marked "ND" and a horizontal arrow marked "RD"; banded features lie oblique to RD. (d) 70%: strongly banded structure, dark etched shear bands cutting many grains. (e) 90%: grains visibly elongated along RD, matrix almost entirely consumed by dark shear bands, with dark strips along the top and bottom edges. Two further panels in the supplied group are not described by the caption: the red-framed magnified inset, and a TEM micrograph labelled (a) with a 500 nm scale bar, green arrows and the label "pile-up" marking dislocation pile-ups at boundaries.
measured_quantities: scale bar length (100 µm for optical panels; 500 nm for the TEM panel)

observations.observation: Panel (a) (10% cold rolling) is an optical micrograph showing equiaxed grains crossed by fine, straight, parallel slip bands, with a visible difference in the distance between slip bands in different grains.
A red-framed inset placed above panel (a) is a magnified view of the region boxed in red in (a), showing slip bands of two orientations intersecting within a grain.
Panel (c) is the only optical panel carrying orientation axes: a vertical arrow marked ND and a horizontal arrow marked RD.
All five optical micrographs (a)-(e) carry a 100 µm scale bar in the lower-right corner.

In panel (e) (90% reduction) the grains are visibly elongated along RD and the dark, banded (shear-band) structure occupies nearly the whole field, whereas the same structure is much less dense in (a)-(c).
The caption labels the five optical micrographs as cold rolling reductions of (a) 10%, (b) 30%, (c) 50%, (d) 70% and (e) 90%.

The citing text divides the microstructure evolution into two stages: stage I (10-50% rolling reduction) is a typical low energy dislocation structure (LEDS) of Taylor-lattice-type produced by planar dislocation glide, with gradual refinement of slip-band spacing.

The citing text states that in stage II (70-90% rolling reduction) abundant shear bands appear and grains are visibly elongated along the rolling direction (RD), the shear bands increasingly eroding the matrix.
The citing text attributes the different slip-band distances in different grains of Fig. 3(a) to inhomogeneous deformation that is more pronounced in favorably oriented grains.
The citing text states that micro-shear bands generated by local strain concentration are extensively observed and accompanied by a rapid increase of the G texture component (Fig. 3(c-e)).

The group as supplied also contains a TEM micrograph labelled (a) with a 500 nm scale bar and green arrows plus the text 'pile-up'; the Fig. 3 caption mentions only optical micrographs, so this panel's provenance is not confirmed by the caption.

subfigures.description: Optical micrograph, 10% cold rolling reduction, 100 µm scale bar. Equiaxed grains with fine straight parallel slip bands; band spacing varies between grains. A red rectangle outlines a region that is magnified in the separate inset.
High-magnification view of the boxed region of (a), showing slip bands of two orientations crossing each other inside a grain. No scale bar or magnification factor is printed on the inset.
subfigures.panel: red-framed inset (magnification of the box in (a))

subfigures.description: Optical micrograph, 30% cold rolling reduction, 100 µm scale bar. Same slip-band morphology as (a) but bands are denser and more numerous within grains; a red rectangle marks an enlarged region.
Optical micrograph, 50% cold rolling reduction, 100 µm scale bar. Arrow axes labelled ND (vertical) and RD (horizontal) define the rolling geometry; dark banded features run oblique to RD.
Optical micrograph, 70% cold rolling reduction, 100 µm scale bar. Dense banded/shear-band structure traversing the grains, markedly darker and more aligned than in (c).
Optical micrograph, 90% cold rolling reduction, 100 µm scale bar. Grains strongly elongated along RD, matrix largely replaced by dark shear bands; dark strips at the top and bottom of the field.

TEM micrograph with a 500 nm scale bar, green arrows and the label 'pile-up' pointing to dislocation pile-ups at boundaries; it is not mentioned in the Fig. 3 caption, which lists only optical micrographs.

unreadable_items: red-framed inset of (a): no scale bar or magnification factor printed, so the magnification is unknown
panel (e): the dark strips at the top and bottom edges are of unclear origin (sample edge vs. heavily etched band)
TEM panel labelled (a): does not belong to the Fig. 3 caption, so its figure/panel provenance is unresolved
